name: html-extract
description: Offline HTML main-content extraction and HTML-to-text/markdown conversion. Given raw HTML, strips script/style/nav/header/footer/aside/comments and decodes entities, then either renders the whole document ('extract: all') or runs a simple readability-style density scan to pick the single best-scoring content subtree ('extract: main', the default). Renders as plain text with block-level newline semantics, or as markdown (headings, lists, links, bold/italic, code blocks). Also returns every link found in the selected content and a word count. Uses a hand-written char-scanner tokenizer, not a real DOM or regex-based HTML parsing, so it tolerates unclosed/malformed tags and runs in linear time on large or adversarial input. Never executes any script/style content — it is discarded unread. Output is bounded: `text` is capped at 400,000 characters and `links` at 2000 entries, with `truncated: true` set if either cap was hit.

html.description: The raw HTML document or fragment to process.

mode.description: 'text' renders plain prose with block-level newlines; 'markdown' additionally renders headings, lists, links and emphasis.

extract.description: 'main' scores container subtrees (paragraph count, comma count, link-density penalty) and keeps only the best-scoring one. 'all' renders the whole stripped document. Defaults to 'all'.

title.description: The document's <title> text, or null if none was found.

truncated.description: true if text was cut at 400,000 characters or links at 2000 entries.
